item.content:encoded:
I think you're misinterpreting this SCP in the extreme. No offense, but the point seems to have gone over your head.

She's not an X-Men villain, she's an otherwise typical SCP who WANTS desperately to be one and has major narcissistic tendencies, so she creates this "super villain" persona for herself. It's more like a gothic teenager trying to get attention by dressing in all black, or someone talking about how deep and dark they are to seem unique. She's not an "out-and-out" X-Men villain- she's a deeply disturbed and selfish individual who happens to have the means to partially fulfill her comic-book fantasies.

In fact, I'm really glad this SCP exists. In all these humanoid SCPs with superpowers we have, doesn't it make sense that at least one would say "Fuck it, I'm a super-hero"? It makes sense. The first thing half of people under 40 would do with SCP-powers is try to fulfill fantasies like this. Give enough people meta-human powers, and one will decide to become a walking comic book character.

She's not a villain. She's playing a game of pretend.

item.content:encoded:
One of the more interesting things I discovered about Vector when I was researching for my crackfic contest entry Lust in the Time of Anomalous Cholera was the extreme lack of background, fanart, or development anywhere. The Escape from Site 19 photo is the best new picture for Vector we have (and it's a great one, not looking to improve on it, except maybe to give her a tattoo down her arm reading, "Where has this needle been?").

But I thought about what we do have, and decided she is Afrikaner. She was searching for Ebola in South Africa, where there is no Ebola. This only makes sense to me if she's actually from South Africa, and just being the useless teen she really is. She was then hiding out in Dresden, which suggests that she would have some connection to Europe to be able to end up there to hide out. Family connection, most likely. Thus, Afrikaner.

So, now I imagine her as this wannabe-villain as played by Yo-Landi Visser of Die Antwoord.

item.content:encoded:
To me the appeal here is all in the Reconstruction. She wants to be a Mary Sue X-Men supervillain, but in reality she is failing epically… and this itself creates an interesting character and situation.

She is exactly what would happen if an teenager with serious emotional issues discovered she had this superpower. Many such teens want to lash out at the world, and this one has the power to do so without a gun. But that doesn't make her any good at it.
Is she dangerous? Without question.
Is she absurdly self-aggrandizing and melodramatic? Absolutely.
Is she competent at being a supervillain? Not in the least.

As the comment below points out, she went to the wrong part of Africa trying to obtain Ebola. She throws a temper tantrum if you don't call her Vector…which the Foundation ignores. Her one big doomsday plot ended with minimal casualties, probably because she picked an "Ebola-Lite" virus that can only be spread by direct contact, has a slow incubation period, and probably incapacitated her when she tried to tinker with it to change either one. Her delusional X-men fantasies slammed smack into realism and the Foundation.

And the icing on the cake: The Foundation's response to her is a combination of "hooray for walking obscure pathogen archive and research center", and "good lord does this girl need to see a psychiatrist."

You know what's always irked me about this article?

SCP-353 was originally encountered in [DATA EXPUNGED], South Africa, where she seemed to be deliberately seeking to pick up strains of the Ebola virus.

There has never been a major Ebola outbreak in South Africa. Ever. The United States has more Ebola cases than South Africa; the recorded Ebola death toll in SA is 1, as in exactly one person. The only place you'll find Ebola in SA is in a secure laboratory. If you wanted to catch that particular virus, you'd go to Gabon, or the DRC.

Now, if you wanted to catch tuberculosis…
